claim.summary: Built the pure §5 claim rules. packages/content/src/claim: claimRules (channelTicks 200 = 10 s x 20, deadlineTicks 42000 = 35 min, circleRadiusTiles 4) with a zod validator (channel 0 allowed as instant victory). packages/simulation/src/claim: createClaimConfig/createClaimState, stepClaim(config, state, tickInput) -> {state, events} in a fixed phase order (reservations, active channel break/advance, start by closest-then-lowest-id, completion, deadline), replayClaim, and the events claim-interrupted/protection-ended/claim-started/claim-completed/duel-ended-without-theft/match-ended. It never mutates its input and freezes after a result. Added one subpath export each (@pirate-sea-race/simulation/claim, @pirate-sea-race/content/claim) and docs/claim.md. Tests: scripted rule tests with deep-frozen inputs, 60 seeded random scripts (at most one winner, frozen after the result, per-tick invariants, replay hashes, every interrupt reason covered), and symmetry tests (input reordering, rotations and mirrors, order-preserving relabelling, a 1000-trial oracle under random relabelling). Executed from this worktree after npm ci: npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run test:unit (425/425 pass), npm run test:integration (22/22 pass), npm run build (exit 0, smoke passed). Also confirmed by hand that both claim subpaths load from dist/, and that the purity test flags a Math.random planted in each new directory (then removed).
open_assumptions: Only the player who actually starts a channel loses protection. A protected player who holds interact while waiting, or who loses a same-tick tie, keeps it. Protection is not read again during a channel.
When the match ends by a completed claim, as well as at the deadline, every encounter still reserved or running is reported as duel-ended-without-theft, because §5 freezes all match outcomes.

A channel starts at progress 0 on its start tick and completes on the channelTicks-th tick after it: interact is held on 201 consecutive ticks, 10 s elapsed. channelTicks 0 completes on the start tick.
'Stopped' means speed 0 and the same position the channel started at. Any drift is 'moved'.
A waiting player may start on the same tick the previous channel breaks, including a break caused by a reservation.
The lowest stable id compares by UTF-16 code units, not by locale or number.
The caller supplies consecutive world ticks; a skipped or repeated tick throws. The treasure-circle radius of 4 tiles is a placeholder tuning value.

findings.message: packages/simulation/src/claim/state.ts createClaimConfig only checks that subUnitsPerTile is a safe integer, not that it is positive. A value of 0 gives circleRadius 0, so only the exact claim point is inside the circle. A negative value gives a negative circleRadius, and insideTreasureCircle squares it, so it silently behaves like a positive circle. stepClaim does not validate a hand-built ClaimConfig either (for example a negative circleRadius or channelTicks). Suggest refusing subUnitsPerTile <= 0 and validating the config's fields.
findings.requirement: inside the treasure circle (a content-defined radius around the final island's claim point)

findings.message: packages/simulation/src/claim/step.ts phase 3 still lets a player start a channel on the deadline tick when channelTicks > 0. Phase 5 cancels it on the same tick, so the caller receives protection-ended, claim-started, claim-interrupted(deadline) and then match-ended. The caller is told to end a player's protection and show a claim for a channel that can never complete. This does not change the outcome, but the events are noisy. Suggest skipping the start phase on the deadline tick unless channelTicks is 0.
findings.requirement: A match that reaches the deadline without a winner ends with no winner.

findings.message: No check verifies that the new subpaths @pirate-sea-race/simulation/claim and @pirate-sea-race/content/claim load from dist/. The postbuild scripts cover only ./duel and ./moves, and scripts/smoke-build.ts reports 8 workspace exports, none of them claim. The build log shows dist compiling but not the subpaths being imported. Only the worker's own statement covers it. decisions.md assigns adding the subpaths to scripts/smoke-build.ts to the assistant at merge, so this is accepted rather than a candidate defect, but it must not be forgotten at merge.

The 'second player waits' tests never use a waiting player who outranks the channeller under the closest-then-lowest-id rule. In packages/simulation/src/claim/claim.test.ts every waiter is farther away ('runs one channel at a time': b at x+1; 'lets a waiting player start...': b at x+100) or ties with a higher id ('keeps the protection of a protected player who must wait': b vs a, both at the claim point). The seeded invariants in determinism.test.ts check that the channeller is eligible and that progress === tick - startTick. Both would still hold if a closer or lower-id newcomer took over the channel. So an implementation that re-applied the ordering rule on every tick and preempted the active channel would pass the whole suite. Add a scripted case where a closer or lower-id eligible player arrives mid-channel and assert that the channel owner and progress are unchanged.
findings.requirement: Only one channel is active at a time; a second eligible player must wait.

findings.message: Non-mutation is tested for the claim state and the tick snapshot, but not for the config. The step() helper in packages/simulation/src/claim/claim.test.ts deep-freezes the input and the state and compares hashState(state) before and after. The ClaimConfig passed to stepClaim is never frozen or compared in any test, including the determinism.test.ts runs. A step that wrote to config (for example to claimPoint) would go undetected.

# Decisions: claim-channel

From the operator session of 2026-09-24. The operator asked for parallel work beside `duel-online`, each run in its own tab. These are the assistant's recommended defaults; no separate grill was held.

## Decisions

- Scope is the pure §5 claim rules with §2's deadline ordering, proven by scripted, symmetry and seeded property tests against §19's "Endgame" gate.
- A separate feature from `objectives-ledger`, so the two run in parallel. "Holds all four types" is an input from the caller, so this feature has no dependency on the ledger.
- The code lives in new directories behind subpath exports (`@pirate-sea-race/simulation/claim`, `@pirate-sea-race/content/claim`). The only shared file is each package's `exports` block, which the assistant reconciles at merge, adding the subpaths to `scripts/smoke-build.ts` at the same time.
- One lane (`claim`), checks typecheck, unit, integration and build, with no browser check.
- The ten-second channel is kept as §5 describes. §5's "test both versions" (a channel versus instant victory on arrival) waits for playtests: the channel length is a content constant, so 0 can model instant victory later.

## Assumptions

- Positions are integer sub-unit coordinates; distance comparisons use squared integer distance, with no square root.
- The caller reports each tick's accepted encounter reservations, disconnects and eligibility.

## Deferred

- Final-island selection, the compass and route reveal, public sector announcements, the claim UI and alarms: `objectives-endgame`.

concerns.message: The acceptance says a player may claim only while 'not protected', yet also that 'starting a claim ends that player's protection first' (§6: claiming ends return protection first and is then processed normally). Protection is an input from the caller, so the claim module cannot clear it. The task doesn't say whether a protected player holding interact starts the channel on that tick (emitting a ProtectionEnded event for the caller) or is refused. It also doesn't say what happens if the caller still reports protected=true on a later tick of an active channel.
concerns.consequence: A worker who reads 'not protected' as a gate will write tests that refuse protected players. Once the room is wired in, returning duel winners and respawned players could never claim unless the room clears protection first, which means rework at integration. A worker who sees the two rules as contradictory may also hit the 'rules contradict' stop and report blocked. Settle it in docs/claim.md: interact while protected emits ProtectionEnded and is then evaluated normally on the same tick; protection is ignored during an active channel.

concerns.message: The channel timing and the deadline tick are not pinned down. Nothing says whether the start tick counts as the first of the 200 progress ticks, whether the match ends at tick == deadline or after it, or whether a CLAIM_CHANNEL_TICKS of 0 (the decisions.md plan for testing instant victory) completes on the start tick.
concerns.consequence: Off-by-one bugs become the tested behaviour. A claim that starts exactly 200 ticks before the deadline can win in one version and time out in another. With a 'progress++ then === length' check, a channel length of 0 never completes, so the promised instant-victory playtest silently hangs. A validator using zod .positive() would reject 0 outright.

concerns.message: Player ids in this codebase are strings (ShipState.id, Colyseus session ids). The rule 'lowest stable player id' needs a defined comparison. localeCompare depends on locale and ICU and is not caught by the purity test. Session ids are also random, so 'lowest' is arbitrary, though deterministic.
concerns.consequence: If the worker uses localeCompare or Intl.Collator, the server and a replay could pick different winners when two claimants tie on distance, and nothing in the checks would flag it. Require plain code-unit comparison (a < b), or the integer slot, and state the choice in docs/claim.md.

concerns.message: 'A duel still running at the deadline is reported as ending without theft' has to come out of a module that only sees a per-player 'reserved for a duel' boolean. It doesn't know the duel ids or pairings, and it has no way to hear about duels that start later. The spec's 'freezes all match outcomes' on a win implies the same treatment for duels running when someone claims the treasure, but the acceptance covers only the deadline.
concerns.consequence: The event will be per player, not per duel, so the room has to deduplicate the pairs. Duels running at the moment of a win have no specified outcome and can later commit a theft after the freeze. Either add an optional duelId to each player snapshot and emit one event per distinct id, sorted, on both the deadline and the win; or record that the room owns this.

concerns.message: The plan doesn't say what happens when the active claimant is missing from a tick's snapshot, or what 'stopped' is based on. It could be an input boolean, a position delta that needs the previous position in state, or ship speed. It also doesn't say whether a waiting player may start on the same tick the active channel resets.
concerns.consequence: Different readings give different same-tick outcomes. For example, B may or may not take over on the tick A moves. The symmetry and replay tests will pass whichever way it goes, so a surprising rule could be locked in without anyone noticing. Write the order of operations explicitly: reservations and resets → completion → starts (tiebreak) → deadline. Treat a missing player as disconnected.

concerns.message: The built subpaths @pirate-sea-race/simulation/claim and @pirate-sea-race/content/claim won't be exercised by the build check in this run. scripts/smoke-build.ts and the postbuild scripts are outside the owned paths, and adding them waits for the merge under decisions.md.
concerns.consequence: A wrong exports entry, such as a dist path typo or wrong condition order, passes every required check here and only fails at merge or when the room imports it. The worker should at least compare the new entries character by character with the ./duel and ./moves pattern.

concerns.message: The seeded random test files live under packages/*/src, and the purity test scans those too. The tests have to use the package's own nextRandom/nextInt from packages/simulation/src/random.ts, not Math.random or a float-based PRNG.
concerns.consequence: If the worker doesn't know this, the first unit run fails the purity test and time goes on rework; a test helper using Math.sqrt for distance fails the same way.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Keep the state to {phase: open|won|timedOut, active: {playerId, progress} | null, winnerId | null}. Each tick the caller passes plain per-player facts: holdsAllFour, inCircle (or a position, compared to the claim point by squared distance), stopped, connected, reserved, protected, holdingInteract and an optional duelId. step() runs a fixed four-stage pipeline: (1) reservations, disconnects and eligibility changes reset the active channel; (2) advance it and complete it when progress reaches the channel length; (3) if no channel is active, start the best starter by (distance², then id by code units); (4) deadline. The event list comes from each stage in a fixed sort order. The claim content module holds only the constants (channel ticks, circle radius, deadline tick) and a validator that allows a channel length of 0. There is no per-player claim state and no queue, which makes the replay-hash and symmetry properties almost trivial.
challenge.cheap_experiment: Before writing step(), spend about 20 minutes writing five boundary scripted cases as a table in docs/claim.md, then pin them as the first tests. (a) The channel starts at deadline−200, −199 and −201 with length 200: which one wins? (b) A reservation lands on the active claimant on the tick their channel would complete. (c) A protected player presses interact with no rival present. (d) Channel length is 0. (e) The active claimant moves on the same tick as two waiting players who are the same distance from the claim point. If any row can't be filled from §2/§5/§6 without guessing, that is the one question to put to the operator. If all rows can be filled, the implementation follows mechanically.

# Task: claim

## Goal

Build the treasure-claim rules of §5 as pure, deterministic code: who may claim, the ten-second channel, everything that interrupts or resets it, and the ordering rules that make simultaneous events and the match deadline come out the same way every time. Later features wire it into the match room. This one only builds and proves the rules.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §5 (all of it), §2 ("Time limits and results": a claim completing on the deadline tick), §6 ("Return to the world": protection rules) and §19 ("Endgame").
- Read `docs/architecture.md`, the existing pure packages (`packages/simulation`: integer state, `hashState`; `packages/content`: rules and validators) and `tests/unit/purity.test.ts`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build`.
- Two other features run at the same time: `duel-online` (most of the repository) and `objectives-ledger` (`packages/simulation/src/objectives`, `packages/content/src/objectives`), which owns rubbing inventories. Stay inside your owned paths.

## Constraints

- Owned paths only: `packages/simulation/src/claim`, `packages/content/src/claim`, `docs/claim.md`, and `packages/simulation/package.json` and `packages/content/package.json` **only to add one subpath export each** (`@pirate-sea-race/simulation/claim`, `@pirate-sea-race/content/claim`, following the existing pattern with the `@pirate-sea-race/source` condition first). Do not change their `postbuild` scripts or dependencies, any existing source file, barrel, tsconfig or root file.
- Do not depend on the ledger: whether a player holds all four types is an input the caller supplies each tick (a boolean per player), so the two features stay independent.
- Pure and integer: no Phaser, Colyseus, DOM, timers, wall-clock time, `Math.random` or floating-point transcendental functions. Time is the world tick (20 per second) supplied by the caller. Durations are named content constants (for example the 10-second channel is 200 world ticks).
- The claim step is a function of (config, claim state, a per-tick world snapshot of the relevant players) that returns a new state and the tick's events. It never mutates its input.
- Out of scope: networking, rooms, rendering, the final-island choice and navigation, encounters themselves (the caller reports accepted encounter reservations), rubbings.

## Acceptance

- **Eligibility** (§5): a player may claim while holding all four types, inside the treasure circle (a content-defined radius around the final island's claim point), stopped, not protected and not reserved for a duel. Starting a claim ends that player's protection first (§6).
- **The channel**: holding interact for 10 seconds completes the claim. Only one channel is active at a time; a second eligible player must wait. Moving, losing eligibility (a lost type), disconnecting or entering a duel resets progress to zero.
- **Completion**: completing commits the winner once and freezes all match outcomes. Inputs arriving after a resolved win cannot cancel it.
- **Same-tick ordering** (§5): each tick processes accepted encounter reservations before advancing claim channels. When several players begin claiming on the same tick, the closest to the claim point wins, then the lowest stable player id. The order players appear in the input never matters.
- **Deadline** (§2): a claim that completes on the deadline tick is processed before the timeout. A match that reaches the deadline without a winner ends with no winner. A duel still running at the deadline is reported as ending without theft (an event for the caller).
- **Tests**:
  - scripted unit tests for every rule above;
  - a symmetry test showing that reordering or relabelling the players gives the same outcome under the ordering rules;
  - seeded random tick sequences showing that at most one winner is ever committed and that the state hashes identically on replay.
- `docs/claim.md` (about a page): the state, the order of operations within a tick, and the events.
- `npm ci` then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build` pass from a clean checkout, and the purity test covers the new directories.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).
- Two rules of §2, §5 or §6 contradict each other in a way that changes this acceptance.
- A check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths.
- After ninety minutes of work, any required check still fails and you cannot name the next fix.

Report `question` only for a choice that would change this acceptance.

open_assumptions: Only the player who actually starts a channel loses protection. A protected player who holds interact while waiting, or who loses a same-tick tie, keeps it. Protection is not read again during a channel.
When the match ends by a completed claim, as well as at the deadline, every encounter still reserved or running is reported as duel-ended-without-theft, because §5 freezes all match outcomes.

A channel starts at progress 0 on its start tick and completes on the channelTicks-th tick after it: interact is held on 201 consecutive ticks, 10 s elapsed. channelTicks 0 completes on the start tick.
'Stopped' means speed 0 and the same position the channel started at. Any drift is 'moved'.
A waiting player may start on the same tick the previous channel breaks, including a break caused by a reservation.
The lowest stable id compares by UTF-16 code units, not by locale or number.
The caller supplies consecutive world ticks; a skipped or repeated tick throws. The treasure-circle radius of 4 tiles is a placeholder tuning value.
